record.title: OpenAI makes the Decisions API generally available for bounded classification, routing and scoring
record.summary: OpenAI made the Decisions API generally available on Oct 22, 2026. The dedicated endpoint turns text, image and JSON inputs into bounded probabilities, choices or scores, currently using GPT-6 Luna; the API guide allows up to 400 questions per request and documents prompt caching and native GPT-Live integration. Decisions and standard GPT-6 Luna uncached input are both listed at $0.10 per million tokens; this endpoint has no output-token charge, while caching discounts and regional/long-context terms also affect cost. OpenAI claims up to 10× lower latency than GPT-6 Luna through Responses API but publishes no workload protocol in the reviewed launch materials. Independent performance, adoption and realized economic effects remain unestablished.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI announced general availability of the Decisions API on 2026-10-22. Its documentation describes POST /v1/decisions, currently supports gpt-6-luna, and returns a probability, a choice among supplied values, or a rubric-based score from text, images and JSON input.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The published API guide allows up to 400 questions in one request and documents prompt caching and native GPT-Live integration. OpenAI lists uncached input at $0.10 per million tokens, cached input at a discounted rate, and no output-token charge for this endpoint; its GPT-6 Luna model page lists the same $0.10 standard uncached input rate, so the endpoint does not reduce the published per-input-token rate. Regional-processing premiums and long-context multipliers can apply.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI says Decisions returns bounded answers up to 10 times faster than GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API. The source does not give a workload, concurrency level, geographic condition, latency statistic or independent benchmark for this comparison.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: No independent latency/accuracy comparison, broad customer adoption, realized cost reduction, or effect on end-to-end workflow outcomes was established in the reviewed sources.

evidence_gaps.description: The up-to-10× speed comparison lacks a public workload and measurement protocol in the reviewed materials, and no independent latency/accuracy comparison was located.

Published token rates do not establish realized customer cost or end-to-end productivity. Decisions has the same listed uncached input rate as GPT-6 Luna; output-token charges, caching, regional/long-context terms and request composition determine any workload-level difference.

brief.importance_rationale: If the advertised speed and input-cost profile holds across suitable workloads, a dedicated bounded-decision endpoint could materially change latency and cost choices in high-volume routing, classification and agent-control paths. This is a useful runtime option rather than a demonstrated field-wide efficiency gain; the product is newly generally available, the comparison protocol is undisclosed, and no independent measurements or adoption outcomes were found.
limitations: All launch and API details are first-party OpenAI statements. Published documentation establishes the offered interface and listed prices, not independent runtime behavior, invoice outcomes or customer performance.
The claimed up-to-10× speed comparison has no disclosed workload or latency statistic in the reviewed sources; it should not be generalized to arbitrary prompts or applications.
Only GPT-6 Luna is documented as supported at launch. Whether typed outputs preserve accuracy for a given application must be evaluated on that task.
Regional-processing premiums, long-context multipliers and cache-write pricing can affect total cost. No workload-level cost calculation is reported here.
No independent adoption, productivity or end-to-end economic effect was found.

The official GPT-6 Luna model page lists the same $0.10 standard uncached input-token rate as the Decisions API. No general input-rate reduction is established; any total-cost benefit depends on output-token savings, caching, request shape and application workload.
brief.summary: OpenAI made the Decisions API generally available on Oct 22, 2026. The dedicated endpoint turns text, image and JSON inputs into bounded probabilities, choices or scores, currently using GPT-6 Luna; the API guide allows up to 400 questions per request and documents prompt caching and native GPT-Live integration. Decisions and standard GPT-6 Luna uncached input are both listed at $0.10 per million tokens; this endpoint has no output-token charge, while caching discounts and regional/long-context terms also affect cost. OpenAI claims up to 10× lower latency than GPT-6 Luna through Responses API but publishes no workload protocol in the reviewed launch materials. Independent performance, adoption and realized economic effects remain unestablished.

technical.claimed_result: OpenAI says the dedicated Decisions endpoint produces bounded answers up to 10 times faster than GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API. The comparison method and workload are not specified in the reviewed announcement or guide.
technical.demonstrated_result: First-party announcement and API documentation specify the generally available endpoint, one supported model, three answer types, supported inputs, up to 400 questions per request, documented GPT-Live integration and listed token pricing. The official GPT-6 Luna page lists the same standard uncached input rate ($0.10 per million tokens) as Decisions; Decisions separately lists no output-token charge. This review did not call the endpoint or measure performance or total workload cost.
technical.mechanism: The API accepts shared text, image or JSON evidence plus typed questions and returns probabilities, a selected allowed value or a score from a rubric. Multiple questions can be batched against shared input, with prompt caching for repeated prefixes and direct triggering from GPT-Live. This narrows the answer format for application decisions instead of generating unrestricted explanatory text.
technical.regime: OpenAI Decisions API as documented on 2026-10-22; currently gpt-6-luna only; bounded probability, choice and score outputs; text, images and JSON; up to 400 questions per request. Pricing and regional/long-context terms follow the first-party guide.
technical.strongest_baseline: OpenAI identifies GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API as the latency comparison. No matched benchmark protocol, accuracy comparison, concurrency, input distribution or uncertainty interval is published in the reviewed sources.

brief.title: OpenAI makes the Decisions API generally available for bounded classification, routing and scoring
brief.why_it_matters: Many agent and application workflows spend time and compute on repeated bounded decisions such as routing, classification and scoring. A specialized endpoint with a published input-only price and a vendor-reported speed advantage could change the cost and latency frontier for those workloads. Whether it improves end-to-end systems depends on task accuracy, concurrency, integration overhead and actual usage; those outcomes are not yet independently measured.
